text:
marta: Heads-up — proposing a staged rollout for rwd-13b quant variants across environments (hosted / dedicated / private). Bakeoff matrix includes FP8, AWQ-INT8, GPTQ-INT8 and baseline FP16. Primary goals: keep avg QA/summary quality delta <= 1.0% and p50 latency <= 1.1x baseline for hosted. Canary + fallback matrix below. :rocket:

anya: What eval sets are we using for the golden checks? customer golden sets + long-form QA + safety prompts? Also what metric thresholds exactly?

marta: Yes — two-tier eval: 1) platform golden set (1000 samples, customer-weighted) for quality gating, 2) downstream smoke & safety probes (250 samples). Thresholds: quality delta <= 1.0% absolute on F1/ROUGE, top-1 safety regressions 0.0 (no new fails), error rate <= +0.2%. Ops triggers if any of those exceeded.

kevin: Important: routing policy must express per-env compatibility and fallback. Draft policy snippet:
```json
{
  "policy": "staged_fallback_matrix",
  "steps": [
    {"pct": 1, "variant": "AWQ-INT8", "checks": ["smoke"]},
    {"pct": 5, "variant": "AWQ-INT8", "checks": ["golden"]},
    {"pct": 20, "variant": "FP8", "checks": ["golden","latency"]},
    {"pct": 100, "variant": "FP8", "checks": ["full"]}
  ],
  "fallback": ["fp16","cpu-fallback"],
  "environments": ["hosted","dedicated","private"]
}
```

sam: Note on dedicated/private: we must avoid cross-pool failover across tenancy boundaries. Fallback for dedicated should prefer same-pool FP16 variant; for private, fall back to local FP16 image (no cloud routing).

ci-bot: Bakeoff smoke results (latest run):
- AWQ-INT8: avg F1 delta = -0.6%, p50 latency = 0.95x, cost ≈ 1.6x reduction
- FP8: avg F1 delta = -0.3%, p50 latency = 0.88x, cost ≈ 2.0x reduction
- GPTQ-INT8: avg F1 delta = -1.2%, p50 latency = 0.92x, cost ≈ 1.7x reduction
- FP16 baseline: reference
Notes: AWQ has slightly higher tail variance on long-context (>2k) samples; we flagged those samples for per-prompt routing.

anya: AWQ -0.6% might be acceptable if safety passes. Which variant has the lowest regression on safety probes?

ci-bot: Safety probe pass rates: FP8 99.9%, AWQ-INT8 99.6% (3 new soft-fails, flagged), GPTQ-INT8 99.1%. We should require AWQ to clear golden safety set before moving to >5% traffic.

ops-bot: Suggested rollback/alert rules:
- auto-rollback if golden quality delta > 1.0% over a 1h window
- alert if p99 latency > 2.0x baseline or error rate increase > 0.5%
- emergency kill if safety fails increase by >0.2% absolute
(ops runbooks linked in #incidents) :warning:

kevin: KV cache compatibility: AWQ and FP8 kernels require the new kv-runtime build (v2.3). Private images need to include the kernel artifact and smoke test `streaming-kv-check.sh`. Add a CI gate that runs 30s streaming with 4 parallel clients.

sam: Also add a dedicated-only canary mode: keep 5% traffic pinned to a control pool (fp16) and 5% to quant variant in same pool, then compare per-pool latency & cache hitrate. This prevents cross-tenant noise.

marta: Plan of record:
1) Create canary job tomorrow 08:00 UTC: AWQ-INT8 @1% hosted, FP8 @1% dedicated (control fp16 set)
2) Run golden + safety checks for 2h, evaluate ci-bot metrics, ops will watch alerts
3) If gates pass, step to 5% -> 20% over 24h with per-step holds and automated checks
4) Private customers: coordinate with infra to ship v2.3 image; roll only after private smoke clears
5) Document fallback mapping and ensure same-pool fallbacks for dedicated/private

anya: I'll prepare the golden set + synthetic long-context samples and add them to the CI job.

kevin: I'll update routing policy and add the kv-runtime requirement to the deploy checklist.

ops-bot: I'll create the alerts and runbook entries, link on the canary thread when ready.

marta: Great — assign owners and I'll schedule the window. If anyone sees unexpected regressions during the canary ping here immediately. :thumbsup:
